newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Troubled Malaysian fundamentalist party soldiers on.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Malaysian fundamentalist party soldiers on.

text.p: Malaysia's fundamentalist Islamic party is trying to maintain its control of the nation's sole opposition state after the defection of a key ally to the government, political analysts said.

The defection of Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah to Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) early this month has brought uncertainty to the Parti Islam se-Malaysia's (PAS) control of northeastern Kelantan state.
Also, relations between the Sultan of Kelantan, a nephew of Razaleigh, and Kelantan chief minister Nik Aziz Nik Mat have cooled since Razaleigh's defection, the analysts noted.
PAS spokesman Subky Latiff said in a telephone interview the party had "some problems" when dealing with the state palace.
"But our grass-roots support is strong," Subky maintained. "We've always been too good to the sultan. Maybe what we need is a hardliner."
Rumours that UMNO was ready to entice elected members of PAS to topple the state government have been swirling since Razaleigh's move, analysts said.

"I think it'll look very bad for both the Sultan and Razaleigh if (UMNO) try to take over Kelantan through non-electoral means," said Jomo Kwame Sundaram, an economics professor with Universiti Malaya and political analyst.

"Although the Sultan is highly respected in Kelantan, so is Nik Aziz," Sundaram told Reuters, adding that any move to oust PAS from the state before the next general elections in 2000 "could cut both ways".
Nik Aziz said on Monday that PAS wishes to be more vigilant with its Islamic policies to retain its influence in Kelantan.
The party had no plans to overturn its ban on liquor, gambling and other vices to endear itself to popular taste, he told journalists at a National Press Club of Malaysia function in Kuala Lumpur.

Nik Aziz said he did not wish to discuss his relationship with the Sultan, but said of Razaleigh: "Everybody knows how principled he is...he slammed UMNO like anything once and now he's back with them."
Kelantan has traditionally been a power base for PAS, except for a respite in the 1980s when it was controlled by the National Front.
In Kelantan, gambling is outlawed, the sale of liquor is banned and even unisex hair salons are not allowed. In September, the government banned the excessive use of lipstick by women.
PAS's stance is at odds with Mahathir's government, which practises a progressive form of Islam that urges Moslems to create wealth in multicultural but predominantly Moslem Malaysia.
Razaleigh, a Kelantan prince, was a senior member in UMNO and in Mahathir's cabinet until a row between them saw him leave UMNO in the 1980s and form the Spirit of 46 party.
Razaleigh helped PAS regain control of Kelantan in the 1990 general elections, but the pact was broken this year.
